candidates.exact_span: The current permit has a TRC limit of 0.019 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the prior enforceable TRC numeric limit; a different reading of whether this limit still applies versus the revised limit would change which numeric criterion is used for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee reported TRC as being present in the effluent.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Indicates reported TRC measurements exist rather than a no-result or no-discharge state; interpretation affects whether an exceedance comparison is performed (A) and how missing-evidence versus reported-result semantics are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: However, the permittee uses potable water for filter backwash, which occurs from once per day to once every three to four days depending on the plant and the time of year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Describes intermittent discharge occurrence tied to backwash operations; different interpretations of when discharge occurs could change whether monitoring was required during specific periods (B) and whether periods without discharge are documented no-discharge or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: According to page 29 of the 2012 NMIP, which states that, "In instances where a facility uses chlorine for disinfection of the wastewater or is used as an emergency back-up to a system using another bacteria control technology such as ultraviolet light, or is used to remove filamentaceous algae, or when chlorine is used to disinfect process equipment used at the facility and the permit writer must limit TRC in the permit."
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the conditional trigger under which a TRC numeric limit must be imposed; whether the facility falls within these chlorine-use instances affects whether an enforceable TRC limit applies (A) and whether associated TRC monitoring obligations are operative (B).

candidates.exact_span: Numeric criteria for Total Residual Chlorine are 19 micrograms per Liter (µg/L) at the point of discharge for Acute Aquatic Life designated uses and 11 ug/L for Wildlife Habitat and Chronic Aquatic Life Designated Uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides alternative WQS-based numeric TRC criteria keyed to designated use; which use applies at the discharge point determines the enforceable limit used for exceedance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: At a stream critical low flow equal to zero (0), the limiting criteria is numeric criteria, which is 11 µg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the flow condition and resulting numeric criterion selection; interpretation of critical low flow and the stated zero-flow assumption changes which TRC limit (11 µg/L versus 19 µg/L) governs compliance.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, TRC limit changed from 0.019 mg/L to 0.011 mg/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States the revised enforceable TRC numeric limit; a different reading of this change would alter the limit against which reported TRC measurements are compared.

candidates.exact_span: Monitoring requirements for the Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) are established in the proposed permit because the discharge enters the Colorado River Basin, in accordance with the current Salinity policy and program outlined in the most current "review, water quality standards for salinity, Colorado river system."
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes that TDS monitoring requirements apply under the proposed permit based on basin and salinity policy; interpretation of this basis affects whether TDS monitoring is required versus report-only or not applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The objective of the policy is to achieve "no salt return" whenever practicable for industrial discharges and an incremental increase in salinity over the supply water for municipal dischargers.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Distinguishes industrial versus municipal salinity control objectives; classification of the Aztec plant under the applicable objective could change which salinity limit or demonstration test governs (A) and what monitoring regime follows (B).

candidates.exact_span: Under the Colorado Salinity Control Program (CSP), the facility is an existing facility where construction commenced on or before October 18, 1975. The Aztec water plant was built in 1954.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classifies the facility as an existing CSP facility based on construction date; different readings of this classification affect which salinity permitting tests and associated limits or monitoring obligations apply.

candidates.exact_span: The applicable test for the Aztec plant is that the existing tonnage of salt is less than one-ton (2000 lbs) per day or 366 tons per year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the operative salt-load numeric test for this facility; interpretation of which test applies and how tonnage is calculated changes the enforceable salinity limit used for compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: TDS data obtained from the DMRs reveals that the discharge does not have a reasonable potential to exceed the 1 ton/day in salinity.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Concludes reasonable potential is absent relative to the 1 ton/day threshold; whether this conclusion is treated as establishing a binding limit exemption or merely supporting rationale affects numeric limit applicability (A) and whether continued monitoring is required (B).

candidates.exact_span: The highest monthly average Total Dissolved Solids reported during the last two years is 19 mg/l.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides the reported concentration input used in salinity and waiver determinations; a different interpretation of which reported value or averaging period applies would change calculated salt load and limit/waiver outcomes.

candidates.exact_span: TDS = 19 mg/l * 8.34 lbs/gal * 0.177 MGD * 1 ton / 2000 lbs = 0.0140 tons/day
candidates.computation_change_reason: Shows the quantitative derivation of daily salt tonnage from reported concentration and flow; interpretation of the flow factor, units, or arithmetic would change whether the discharge is below the 1 ton/day enforceable threshold.

candidates.exact_span: Since the TDS concentration is less than 500 mg/L, the discharge qualifies for a "fresh water waiver" irrespective of the total daily or annual or annual salt load.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a concentration-based waiver that may supersede salt-load limits; whether the waiver is operative distinguishes enforceable numeric salinity limits from waived/report-only treatment (A) and alters applicable monitoring obligations (B).

candidates.exact_span: Furthermore, the reported TDS is less than 1 ton/day, monitoring shall continue to be performed once every three months, using grab sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies continued quarterly grab-sample TDS monitoring conditioned on reported salt load; interpretation of this requirement affects whether monitoring was obligatory (B) and how periods without reported results are classified when monitoring was still required (C).

candidates.exact_span: The dissolved Oxygen criteria according to 20.6.4.900.H (4) NMAC for warmwater, marginal warmwater and coolwater aquatic criteria are respectively 5 mg/L or more.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States the numeric dissolved oxygen criterion and designated-use categories; which aquatic-life classification applies determines the enforceable DO limit used for any reported measurement comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Since the facility is a water Treatment Plant, DO modeling is not required.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Exempts DO modeling for this facility type; interpretation of whether modeling versus direct monitoring is required affects evaluated monitoring obligations (B) and how absent DO results are characterized when modeling is not the expected evidence type (C).
